items.headline: Israel's vote count leaves Netanyahu and rivals short of a majority
items.summary: Israelis turned out in their highest numbers in decades on Tuesday, lifting opposition hopes of unseating Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. With no bloc assured of a majority, forming the next government could take weeks or months of coalition talks.

items.headline: Bolsonaro's party accepts Lula's win as Flávio refuses to concede
items.summary: Brazil's main opposition party accepted President Lula da Silva's runoff victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro still has not conceded and President Trump called the vote rigged without evidence. Lula told supporters the election was a defeat for lies.

items.headline: Justice Department suit over Alaska Senate race draws scrutiny
items.summary: A Justice Department lawsuit seeks to block certification of Alaska's Senate race. The Nation's Elie Mystal argues the case signals the administration will not accept midterm results Republicans lose.

items.headline: Southwest flood damage runs to hundreds of millions in New Mexico
items.summary: Intense rainstorms linked to an El Niño-driven Pacific hurricane season have displaced thousands of people across the Four Corners states. Damage estimates for New Mexico alone run to hundreds of millions of dollars.

items.headline: Judge halts Trump's D.C. golf course overhaul
items.summary: A federal judge barred the government from clearing trees or altering East Potomac Park without proper notice. President Trump said the work will still start next month and the administration will appeal.

items.headline: Violence overshadows student-led protests in France
items.summary: Largely peaceful demonstrations in France were overshadowed by violence and property destruction in the streets of Paris and Limoges. The Nation's correspondent described the unrest as hijacked by agitators.

items.headline: Industry knew for decades microplastics could enter the body
items.summary: An investigation found the chemical industry has known for decades that ingested microplastic particles can reach vital organs. Yale Environment 360 reported the findings on Tuesday.

items.headline: Aldi's low prices push grocery rivals to respond
items.summary: The German-owned grocery chain is winning over U.S. shoppers with low prices. Competitors are being pushed to respond, NPR's Planet Money reported.

items.headline: Nairobi's 'Green Army' prepares for El Niño floods
items.summary: In flood-prone Nairobi, workers known as the Green Army are preparing to head off disaster before El Niño rains arrive. The effort is part of the city's push to adapt to more extreme weather.

items.headline: Mbappé apologizes after calling Mao a dictator
items.summary: French soccer star Kylian Mbappé apologized after a comment calling Mao Zedong a dictator drew backlash in China. TIME explained the controversy on Wednesday.

digest.overview:
The Supreme Court declined to restore immigration judges' power to administratively close deportation cases. A federal judge in Los Angeles sounded skeptical of the Justice Department's bid to set aside nearly 20,000 county mail ballots and said he would rule Wednesday. The department gave Washington state until noon Wednesday to stop counting ballots from more than 400 people it says may be noncitizens. Alaska asked a federal judge to dismiss the department's suit over certifying its Senate race, calling it baseless. Prosecutors filed a new charging document against James Comey to extend a statute of limitations, which he called an appalling abuse. Trump campaigned in Texas with Senate nominee Ken Paxton as more than 30 million Americans have already voted. New Mexico's governor said flood damage there could reach $200 million to $300 million.

Abroad, Israel's count left neither camp with a majority: with about two-thirds tallied, Ynet put Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc at 54 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's at 48 and Arab parties at 18, short of the 61 needed. Citing the Wall Street Journal, Ynet reported that Washington urged Gulf states to prepare for a short but intense campaign against Iran after the midterms. Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with a ballistic missile and 88 drones. Brazil's Federal Police said Flávio Bolsonaro left the country despite a court travel ban. South Korea's Supreme Court ordered former first lady Kim Keon Hee held two more months, and SK Hynix topped 100 trillion won in quarterly revenue for the first time. China's Communist Party plenum enters its final days. The World Meteorological Organization said carbon dioxide levels reached 426.8 parts per million in 2025.

home.overview:
Tampa Bay is still alive: the Rays beat Milwaukee 4–3 in 12 innings on Ben Williamson's bases-loaded walk-off single, after Cooper Pratt's homer had put the Brewers ahead in the top half, cutting the World Series lead to 3–1 before Game 5 tonight at Tropicana Field. Jayson Tatum poured in 40 and beat the overtime buzzer as Boston edged Brooklyn 125–124, the Knicks finally won, 111–97 over Detroit, and Portland stayed perfect with a 136–129 win at the Lakers, while Minnesota's Anthony Edwards heads for knee surgery. In the NFL, Indianapolis sold off two stars in a day, sending Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco, before Week 8 opens Thursday with Panthers at Packers.

League Two Fleetwood stunned 10-man Arsenal on penalties, 5–3 after a 1–1 draw, in the Carabao Cup fourth round, and Bradford beat Peterborough 2–0; Liverpool host Chelsea tonight. Bayern's Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or, the first Englishman in 25 years, ahead of Saturday's Der Klassiker against Dortmund, while MLS stages 14 midweek games tonight. In the KBO, Samsung beat Kia 8–3 behind 42-year-old Choi Hyoung-woo's homer to level their second-round series 1–1, with Game 3 Thursday in Gwangju.

brief: Samsung beat Kia 8–3 in Game 2 in Daegu on Tuesday to even the best-of-five second round at 1–1.
Ariel Jurado allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings to earn the win and game MVP honors.
Choi Hyoung-woo, 42, went 2-for-3 with a solo homer and two RBIs, setting KBO postseason age records, and Lewin Diaz hit a two-run homer.
Game 3 is Thursday at 6:30 p.m. KST in Gwangju, with Keisho Shirakawa expected to start for Kia and Choi Won-tae for Samsung.
The series winner faces regular-season champion KT Wiz in the Korean Series.

brief: Tampa Bay beat Milwaukee 4–3 in 12 innings on Tuesday to avoid a World Series sweep and cut the Brewers' lead to 3–1.
Cooper Pratt homered in the top of the 12th to put Milwaukee ahead before Jonny DeLuca's single tied it and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson won it with a bases-loaded single.
David Hamilton's solo homer in the fifth had tied the game 2–2, and neither team scored again until the 12th.
Game 5 is tonight at 8 p.m. ET at Tropicana Field, with Jacob Misiorowski expected to start for Milwaukee and Nick Martinez for Tampa Bay.
If needed, the series returns to Milwaukee for Game 6 on Friday and Game 7 on Saturday.
